approvedDesign.title: A trap A: when the written work is done and the squad reaches the way home, 3 veteran ambushers appear in sight and killing them is added to the terms
approvedDesign.problem: TWISTS.trap (missiontypes.js:835) is rolled at weight 6 and pays x1.5, and no code reads it (field.js traps() at 1837 is the dungeon structure kind 'trap', unrelated). The card promises a change of terms partway in. The only code that rewrites terms mid-run is Hardcore's escalate(). Squads finish early (escort at 0.2 to 0.3 of the estimate, recon at 0.5 to 1.0), so a trigger set as a fraction of the estimate would often fire after the squad has left, or never.
evidence: missiontypes.js:835 TWISTS.trap: weight 6, reward 1.5, only recon, escort, expedition, retrieval, pursuit; no consumer. missiontypes.js:965 and sortie.js:679 pay the x1.5 today with no effect in the run.

field.js:1562 escalate() rewrites m.win, resets s.phase and the portal; it is saved because save() (2004) stores s.mission and s.escalated. field.js:1323 workDone, 1303 inPortal, 1334 squadPoint; step() runs overtime(s) then leave(s) at 2148-2149, so a hook between them acts before anyone is extracted.
field.js:1519-1524 rawWin: 'eliminate' is met when every actor named w is dead; LATCHING is {reach} only (1507). Terms already met stay met without a latch reset; the new atom is the only unmet one.

field.js:1687 makeActor names a species through s.name (FieldView.namer, fieldview.js:50, which honours a species already set); field.js:1970 ACTOR_KEYS already saves name, grade, species, found, lastSeen, lastAt.

field.js:778 a hostile notices at dist2 < sight and canSee; 808 under 'ambush' pressure a hostile moves only while it sees the squad. A mark placed 8-11 tiles away behind cover was never engaged: 17 of 762 sprung runs of the first prototype ended 'this is going nowhere' (ABANDON, field.js:1662), e.g. retrieval seed 6404551 and recon seed 1353802.

field.js:730 chooseGoals reads detailFor() before taskGoal(); tactics.js:259 propose() returns null when phase is 'leaving', so a stand raised against the ambushers is never ended once the kill flips the phase. 26 of 762 sprung runs of the first prototype ended 'the work was done and they never got home' (expedition seed 6122040: squad on tile (7,2), goal 'point', 1000 s, portal at (1,4)). See terrain-leaving-clears-details; with it, 0 of 765 sprung runs end that way.

field.js pressure 'quarry' (pursuit) makes a role 'mark' flee to far-exit and escapes() removes it, so the term would never be met; the ambushers are role 'hostile' named 'ambusher'. With role 'mark' and a ring of 8-11 tiles, escort ended 227 of 240 won, with 2 ABANDON stalls.

u-retreat is in the tree: field.js:1477 contacted(), 1487 retreat(), sortie.js:538 exitState (free, order, retreating, stuck). The ambushers see the squad the step after they appear, so the button reads 'Order a retreat'.

sortie.js:138 fighterFor returns null for an actor with no species and sortie.js:166 pacifies a skirmish with an empty side for 120 s, so a ward is never fought over; hostiles pick targets from the squad (chooseGoals). The escort loss in the first proposal (100% to 79%) was measured on the attrition runner and is not reproduced here.

Measured on test/sortie.harness.js (method as storm-a, GEAR=1, levels 2-4, SEED 1), 5 eligible types x 240 paired contracts, details fix on in both arms. Baseline 67.8% wins, 0.207 deaths per run; trap with 3 veteran ambushers 55.5%, 0.247; paired -12.3 +/-0.9 points of wins, +0.040 +/-0.006 deaths. The trap sprang in 765 of 1200 runs (64%); the other 36% fail or withdraw before reaching the way home with the work done (baseline 11% wins there). Among sprung runs: wins 100% to 80.7%, deaths per run 0.024 to 0.086. By type among sprung: escort 80% (0.07 deaths), expedition 86% (0.07), pursuit 84% (0.04), recon 69% (0.20), retrieval 83% (0.07). Survivors under 40% hp at their lowest: 16.5% to 23.1%. Ambusher distance at the spring: mean 6.1, 2 to 8 tiles. Spring time / estimate p50 0.44, p99 1.09, max 1.39 (ABANDON is 2.5).

Dial, same harness: 1 veteran R 0.963 (wins -1.2 +/-0.3, deaths +0.003); 2 veterans R 0.970 (-4.3, +0.013); 3 veterans R 1.098 +/-0.024; one grade above the paper's top (elite at levels 2-4) R 1.90 (-25.0 +/-1.2, deaths +0.30); a copy of the weakest hostile group on the paper R 1.045 +/-0.015, of the strongest R 1.105 +/-0.022 (7 to 8 basics on expedition, none on escort or pursuit). Cast top grade by level, 40 rolls x 5 types: veteran 97% at levels 1-4, 76% at 5-6, elite 62% at 8, elite or ancient from 10. At level 7 with the same squads (baseline 21.5% wins, 1.23 deaths) a single cast-top ambusher took sprung wins from 98.8% to 22.5%.

Retreat order at the spring (same runs, retreat ordered the step the ambushers appear): sprung wins 31.9%, deaths per sprung run 0.046; fighting on: 80.7%, 0.086. Details fix off: 16 'never got home' and 3 'could not get clear' among 761 sprung runs, R 1.128.

Field.save at the spring, JSON round trip, Field.restore: 53 of 53 sprung runs finished with the amended terms and no second spring (7 of 60 ended before a spring), plain attrition resolver, 5 types x 12 seeds.
approvedDesign.change:
ALTERNATIVE TO trap-b (dropped; this is the only trap design). Sequenced after u-honesty (modsOf, MOD_TEXT) and terrain-leaving-clears-details; u-retreat is already in the tree.

MODS ENTRY.
trap: { label: 'A trap', weight: 6, reward: 1.10, only: ['recon', 'escort', 'expedition', 'retrieval', 'pursuit'], trial: false, mods: { ambush: { count: 3, grade: 'veteran', ring: 0.65 } } }
modsOf takes the first ambush found (no stacking). Generated tooltip: 'When the written work is done and the squad reaches the way home: 3 veteran hostiles appear in sight, 65% of sight range to one tile inside it (6 to 8 tiles; 3 to 4 at night), and Kill the 3 ambushers is added to the terms. Nothing else on the map changes.' grade is data: 'veteran', another grade id, or 'cast' (the highest grade among the written cast's hostile, patrol and mark groups).

TRIGGER (one predicate for gate, window and standfast exits): mods.ambush && !s.trapped && !s.withdrew && !s.escalated && !s.skirmishes.length && workDone(s) && squadOn(s).some(a => inPortal(s, a)), evaluated each step between overtime(s) and leave(s). A squad that has broken off is not ambushed; a Hardcore contract that has escalated is not.

CONSUMERS, by file and function.
1. missiontypes.js: the row; the modsOf default (ambush null); ATOM_TEXT.eliminate (1005) prints 'Kill the N whos' when a.count > 1; rollTwists trial filter (shared with storm-a); MOD_TEXT.ambush.
2. field.js: start() sets s.mods and s.trapped = null; restore() derives mods from the saved mission and reads o.trapped; save() writes trapped. trapTick(s) is called in step() between overtime(s) and leave(s). springTrap(s): ringTile(s, c, lo, hi) picks a passable tile reachable from the entry (map.dist >= 0) at Chebyshev distance lo..hi from squadPoint(s) with a line of sight to it (canSee), where hi = sight - 1 (hostiles notice at dist2 < sight) and lo = max(2, round(ring x sight)); if none, lo falls to 2; if still none the step is retried and after 30 tries s.trapped = { at, none: true } and nothing happens. For each of count ambushers: makeActor({ role: 'hostile', grade, name: 'ambusher', side: 'theirs' }, tile, s) with found = true, lastSeen = clock, lastAt = squad point. m.win gets { ...MT.OBJ.eliminate('ambusher'), count, amended: true } inserted before the walk-home atom; s.doneAt = null, s.phase = 'in', s.pushed = false; a gate portal returns to closed with progress 0; s.trapped = { at, id, grade, n, species, dist }. Log: 'trap: <species> (veteran) is <d> tiles from the squad; terms now: <terms>' (N lines are not repeated).
3. u-retreat: no edit. contacted() turns true the step after the spring (the ambushers spot the squad, field.js:878), so exitState reads 'order'; a squad that has not been spotted before could still call it off for that one step.
4. sortie.js: renderSide (1625) prefixes an atom with amended: true with a warning mark; the card tooltip and the per-twist record as in storm-a. fieldview.js drawActors (213): a red ring on live hostiles named 'ambusher'.
5. Tests: see TESTS.

CARD AND MAP. Card: tag 'A trap' with the generated tooltip, 'A trap x1.10' in the itemised pay; the brief does not list the ambushers (they are not in m.cast, so describe().hostiles and Bestiary.brief are unchanged). Map: at the spring ringed tokens appear in sight, the side panel adds the new term with a warning mark, the log gives species, grade, count and distance, and the button reads 'Order a retreat'.

DECISION. Before launch: arrive at the way home with hp and pools left, so healers, a fifth member, or skipping the contract. During the run: at the spring, fight on or order a retreat. Measured on sprung runs: fighting on wins 80.7% with 0.086 deaths; ordering the retreat at once wins 31.9% with 0.046 deaths. At the harness's win fee of 176 gems and 100 gems per death, fighting on is worth about 86 gems more in pay and costs about 4 gems more in deaths, so the retreat is the right call only for a squad that is already hurt, which the player reads from the squad list. broken() still withdraws an exhausted squad on its own.

RETREAT, WOUNDS, DEATH. Retreat: a retreat ordered at the spring is a loss and the ambushers hunt the squad on the walk (0.046 deaths per sprung run). Wounds: survivors under 40% hp at their lowest 16.5% clear, 23.1% trap (u-wounds injury trigger). Permadeath: +0.040 +/-0.006 deaths per run, 0.086 per sprung run, 0.20 on recon.

REWARD x1.10. R = 1.098 +/-0.024 with the formula of storm-a. Inputs, n = 1200 pairs: p0 0.678, p1 0.555, W0 176 gems, L0 48.7, L1 64.9 (the ambushers' drops are paid), d0 0.207, d1 0.247. Rounded to the nearest 0.05. The current 1.5 is 0.4 above it. Check on screen: base pay line, the 100-gem Summon button, the per-twist record 'with A trap: N sent, W won, D lost'; test/contracts.js recomputes R from 400 fixed-seed sorties per arm and fails when the row is more than 0.10 below. The price is measured at levels 2-4 only (see risks).

FREQUENCY. Weight 6, only the five types: 1.8%, 3.7%, 5.5% of first draws for those types at levels 1, 10, 18 under the honesty draw rule, about 1.2% of all contracts at level 10; the spring fires in 64% of those.

TESTS. test/trap.js: Field.play with the twist forced, 5 types x 40 seeds: s.trapped set in at least 55% of runs; ambushers have role 'hostile', name 'ambusher', found true, distance 2 to sight - 1 and a line of sight at spawn; m.win holds one amended eliminate before the walk-home atom; Field.save at the spring, JSON round trip, Field.restore finishes with the amended terms and no second spring; a withdrawn squad never springs; no run ends with an open detail after phase 'leaving'. Reproduce the price: TWISTS=none vs TWISTS=trap, TYPES=recon,escort,expedition,retrieval,pursuit GEAR=1 LEVEL=2-4 RUNS=240 SEED=1 node test/sortie.harness.js run, then diff.
approvedDesign.playerEffect: The contract has a second act that the written terms did not describe, and it arrives when the squad has finished and used its hp. The player decides how much to hold back: a healer, a fifth member, or another contract. The retreat button has a concrete moment to be used, with the cost of using it on the screen (31.9% wins and 0.046 deaths against 80.7% and 0.086). The cost varies by type: recon (69% among sprung runs, 0.20 deaths) is hit hardest, escort (80%) and the others lose 14 to 17 points.
approvedDesign.secondOrder: Wounds deepen after a trap (16.5% to 23.1% of survivors under 40% hp), which feeds u-wounds recovery time and the debrief's ready-in figure. Tactics responds with its own stand or pounce on the ambushers and now ends it (terrain-leaving-clears-details). The ambushers' species is recorded by Bestiary.record, so the town learns it. Positive levelOffset is not used (the engine's SWARMED assumes non-positive). If Reinforcements or Hunted are approved they can share ringTile.
approvedDesign.risks: The price is measured at levels 2-4 with 3-5 star squads. The paper's top grade steps from veteran to elite around level 8, a single cast-top ambusher is priced at about 1.9 at levels 2-4, and at level 7 the same squads (21.5% baseline wins) cannot be priced; so grade is fixed at veteran, which is the safe error: at levels where veterans are the rank and file the trap costs less than 1.10 and the player is overpaid. A level-aware row (grade 'cast', count by band) needs a matched-squad harness at levels 8 and up. 36% of contracts never reach the way home with the work done and pay no premium. Ambushers appear in sight, so a squad that has already run its tactics plan may stand against 3 hostiles in a doorway; that is the intended fight. A run saved before the build with the trap id and the work done will spring on reload. Wave 1 and 2 are editing field.js and sortie.js; line numbers move.
approvedDesign.response: Design (rework). Explain the escort loss with a log sample: in the combat-backed harness escort goes 100% to 96% with one veteran and 100% to 80% among sprung runs with three; the 21-point loss in the first proposal came from the attrition runner and is not reproduced, and 'the ward stands in the fight' is not the cause (the ward has no fighter and is never targeted: sortie.js:138, 166). The stalls in the first prototype had two causes found in logs: an ambusher outside sight or not found under 'ambush' pressure (17 ABANDON runs; recon seed 1353802, retrieval seed 6404551) and a Tactics stand that the phase change never ended (26 runs; expedition seed 6122040, pursuit seed 5268370). Both are fixed (placement in sight with found = true; the details fix), and role 'hostile' avoids the mark's flee behaviour under quarry pressure. Grade from the cast: tested and declined as the default (evidence 12): a single cast-top ambusher prices at 0.96 for veterans and about 1.9 for the grade above, and at level 7 it cannot be priced with these squads, so grade is data, fixed at veteran, with 'cast' available; count 3 is the dial that gives 1.10. trial: false: accepted. Log line states the mechanic: accepted (species, grade, count, distance, terms). Keep weight 6: kept. 'One rational answer in the run': with three ambushers the retreat saves 0.04 deaths per sprung run and gives up 49 points of wins, so the answer depends on the squad's state, which is the point. 'Generic pre-launch lever': the picker has no per-contract hint, and I do not add one. Engineering (rework). ABANDON re-arm: the spring is at most 1.39 x the estimate and ABANDON is 2.5 x, and no sprung run ended 'going nowhere' after the placement fix, so no offset is added; doneAt restarts at the spring. Escort and ward delivery: the predicate counts squad members only and escort stays in the list on the measured 80%. Sequencing after u-honesty and u-retreat: accepted (u-retreat is in the tree). Price reproduced on test/sortie.harness.js: done (evidence 10, 11).

verdicts.attack: A single veteran at mission level against a squad that has just finished the job is won 88% of the time; the mid-run 'decision' (retreat = certain loss, fight = 88% win) has one rational answer, so nothing is decided during the run and the pre-launch lever (bring a healer) is the generic one. The escort loss (100% to 79%) is attributed to 'the ward stands in the fight', which the code does not support: the ward has no fighter (sortie.js:133) and is dropped from the party list and the dead list (sortie.js:155-156, 180). The likelier cause is a stall: escort's pressure is 'ambush' (missiontypes.js:411), under which a hostile moves only while it sees the squad (field.js:805), while guard orders leash every squad member within 2 tiles of the ward (field.js:738-740), so a mark spawned 8-11 tiles away behind cover never closes and the squad never reaches it; the run then ends by ABANDON or the doneAt rule, which is minutes of nothing on screen and a loss. Fixed grade 'veteran' makes the twist weaker as level rises and the price drifts. Pay drops 1.5 to 1.15 on 1.2% of contracts: the player will not notice the tag.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS.trap missiontypes.js:835 (weight 6, x1.5, five types) with no consumer; traps() field.js:1812 is structure kind 'trap', unrelated; escalate() rewrites m.win/lose/bonus/duration/exitMode/orders/pressure and is saved with s.mission (field.js:1537-1561, 1982); workDone :1321, inPortal :1301, portalTick :1353, leave :1857 and the step order portalTick/overtime/leave :2118-2120; makeActor :1662 names via s.name, raise :1154, spawnGroup :1648; Bestiary.brief reads hostile/patrol/mark groups of cast only (bestiary.js:204-205); strikeTarget matches role, name or kind (tactics.js:201-212); descend() refuses while skirmishes are open (field.js:1763). Scratchpad proto/exp holds real.js, t2.js and the patched field.js; the 750-run trap table was not found as a file, so those figures are unverified beyond the method existing.
verdicts.demand: Explain the escort loss with a log sample before escort stays in 'only'; if it is the ambush-pressure stall, give the mark an unconditional hunt (the same march flag reinforcements-a adds to chooseGoals) or drop escort. Set the mark's grade from the cast (the cast's top grade, or NATIVE(lv)+1) so it stays a threat at every level, and re-measure the price. Add trial: false. Keep weight 6. The log line must state the mechanic ('veteran <species> spawned 9 tiles away; new term: kill the target'), not 'The paper was wrong'.

verdicts.attack: Re-arms the abandonment rule: springAmbush sets s.doneAt = null, and verdict() withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (field.js:1636); a squad that reaches the way home late (the builder's own recon p90 is 1.01 of the estimate; ABANDON is 2.5) is pulled out at the spring instead of fighting. The mark is fixed at 'veteran' with GRADE_BUMP 0 (sortie.js:27), while NATIVE(lv) (missiontypes.js:286) makes veterans the rank and file from level 6 and elites from 12, so the ambusher is weaker than one written body from level 6 on and the twist decays to nothing while still paying 1.15; the scratchpad springA already derives the grade from the cast's top grade and the proposal discards that. On escort the ward can be delivered a step before the first squad member enters the ring (leave() :1895-1900 extracts the ward on inPortal; the predicate counts squad members only), so the 'ward in the fight' claim holds only sometimes and escort still loses 21 points. Depends on u-honesty (mods) and u-retreat (contacted/exitState), neither built.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS.trap at :835; escalate :1537-1561 rewrites win/lose/bonus/duration/exitMode/orders/pressure, resets latched/phase/pushed, raises and respawns; save() stores mission and escalated (:1975-1999); workDone :1321; inPortal :1301; portalTick :1353; leave :1857; step order portalTick/overtime/leave at :2118-2120; makeActor :1662 names through s.name; raise :1154; spawnGroup :1648; bestiary.js:205 brief reads hostile/patrol/mark only; tactics.js strikeTarget :201-203 reads eliminate/subdue atoms; matches() :98 by role, name or kind so name 'target' works; OBJ.eliminate exists and objectiveText prints 'Kill the target'. The scratchpad field.js carries trapReady/springA/trapTick as described and exp/roundtrip.js exists. Not found: the 750-run and 500-run trap result tables (72.0%, 0.053, 591 sprung, elite 54.6%/0.260); proto/out holds only storm files, so those figures are unverified prototype printouts.
verdicts.demand: Sequence after u-honesty and u-retreat. Record the spring time and exclude it from the ABANDON test (or restart that clock at the spring). Make the grade data that follows the contract (cast top grade or NATIVE(lv)+1) and re-measure the price at levels 6 and 12. Drop escort from only, or make the predicate include the ward's delivery. Put the trap measurement in a results file and reproduce it on test/sortie.harness.js before 1.15 is fixed.

sharedRules: Shared rules the user approved for every complication: (1) one price rule: the multiplier keeps expected gems per attempt equal, counting a death at PULL_COST (100 gems), R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), rounded up to the next 0.05; (2) every number is re-measured on test/sortie.harness.js (add TWISTS=, GEAR=1 options if missing), not on a private runner; (3) at most one body-adding complication per contract (reinforcements, hunted, trap, turncoat, infested) until pairs are measured; (4) log lines state what spawned, where, at what distance and which term changed, in the engineering register; (5) trial: false on every row that adds bodies, threaded through quests.js.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

u-retreat's contacted() is extended three ways: trap-a adds !!s.trapped, reinforcements-a mirrors it with s.contactAt set in look() and openSkirmish(), hunted pre-marks followers spotted to stay out of it; one definition of contact, in one place, before any of these.

MOD_TEXT shape. u-honesty specifies a static table keyed by mod; terrain and arrivals generate per-contract text (member lines, 'x bodies on this paper', species tags), so the honesty API must take (mods, mission) before these build; infested-b's and reinforcements-a's cards cannot be produced from the static table.

All three lenses say wave 1 is editing field.js, sortie.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js. Wave 1 is finished (.team-backup/r1w1, project files dated 01:xx-03:06); wave 2 started at 03:09 (.team-backup/r1w2) and holds u-honesty, u-retreat, u-wounds, u-ledger, u-readout and u-debrief, which touch every file these twelve cite. Every line number here moves before any of them builds, and none lists after: ['u-honesty', 'u-retreat'] in a form the scheduler reads.
missed: u-honesty is approved but not built: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, MT.factors or TWIST_FULL (grep across *.js is empty) and its spec moves the six rows out of TWISTS into a comment block. All twelve proposals write MODS entries against that API and re-add rows it removes; none states the dependency as a build order, and a builder landing before it would write a second, incompatible fold.

None of the three lenses used test/sortie.harness.js (u-harness, approved and present: boots game.html's script list through test/game.boot.js and plays real Sortie launch/skip/settle with combat.js, gear, potions, Condition pools and Outfit). Each wrote a private runner that re-implements resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast with gearless parties; every absolute death rate is an upper bound by the builders' own admission, and every multiplier is priced on those numbers. The field-balance-harness memory says to quote game figures from sortie.harness.js.

Storm and the window clock: escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage and capture carry deadline: true (missiontypes.js:409, :524, :595, :618, :640, :708), exitFor (:195) gives them the window exit, and shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313). Walking x0.8 shortens the usable window by 20% on six types; neither storm design scales or discloses it (only Hardcore's escalate seconds are scaled).

escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch (:1373-1376) respawn 50% / 30% of every hostile and patrol spawn group with no check for deferred, at, arrive or follows, so any twist that adds a cast group gets it cloned on escalation and on every window shut. reinforcements-a skips its groups; hunted-a and hunted-b do not.

Stale offers: boards re-roll every 6 minutes (sortie.js:97) but trial offers persist per character until the star changes (quests.js:112); any twist that changes the cast at roll time (reinforcements-a/b, infested-a/b, hunted-a/b) leaves already-rolled offers carrying the tag with no bodies behind it and the multiplier still applied. Only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check.

describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast; the card's hostile figure includes a column or follower unless excluded. hunted-a excludes follows groups; reinforcements-a/b do not.

combat.js types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type (:303) and its splash as 'arcane' (:308); storm-a's per-type damage multiplier misses heat splash. Riposte (:215) uses the target's damageType and DoT (:593) the condition's type, so those paths are covered.

trap-a sets s.doneAt = null at the spring; verdict() (field.js:1636) withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (2.5), so a late squad is pulled out at the moment the ambush appears.

The measured cost of hunted-a, hunted-b and part of reinforcements-a is a body on the route home (hunted-a: 49 of 52 follower-fight deaths after leaving; hunted-b: 84 of 86; reinforcements-a: 26% of firings after the walk home starts), while the tooltips describe triggers (HP under 70%, commit at 60%, contact + 45 s) that the builders' own sensitivity tables show barely move the outcome. Under the traceable-numbers rule the card has to name the thing that costs.

Positive levelOffset is new to the engine: SWARMED (field.js:84) clamps it to 0.15 and feeds makeActor hp/power (:1682-1683) and every odds() call tactics makes; infested-a includes the fix, but nothing else that reads levelOffset was audited for the sign (bestiary brief, noteSighting and castLevel add it correctly; the plain harness and tactics tests assume it is negative).

Perf was measured for one proposal only (infested-b: hostiles per run 13 to 24, 35 at level 8, Node only). turncoat-b puts an actor scan under found()/known() (10 call sites in field.js, several inside per-actor filters per step); trap-b rebuilds the map mid-run; reinforcements-b scans the whole tile grid once per call. None was timed in the browser.

Evidence slips that do not change verdicts but should be corrected in the specs: terrain's fire-word class list (classes.js has mastery 'fire' in grenadier :466, artillerist :566 and kineticist :999, not arcanist or elemental_mage; the picker line must come from Classes.lexiconOf at classes.js:1818, which the proposal does name); pursuit's 'quests.js:116 passes trial: true' (it passes level and name only); the 1950-run storm figures and all trap figures are not in any results file in the scratchpad (proto/out holds storm_random.txt at n=1500 with different death rates, storm_b_wet.txt and storm_b_cands.txt), while every pursuit log and the arrivals final-n100 files reproduce the quoted numbers.
